answer: A farm running 184 keys therefore pays that exposure on every endorsement it manufactures, which removes the asymmetry that normally makes mass attestation cheap. Because the shale stake is held until the horizon settlement, the operator carries real capital per endorsement, and the marble audit lists each exposure. An attester must stake 39% of the reward its attestation would unlock, so endorsing a high-value answer costs proportionally more than endorsing a cheap one. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
